clue.text: Card presented by the stable worker, a brash young man

parts.note: a jack is a playing card, the knave
taken as written
a lad is a stable boy who looks after racehorses

explanation.surface: A card game in which a stable hand shows his cheeky side.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is British slang for a cocky, flashy young fellow who enjoys showing off.

clue.text: Soldier, possibly. — one taking canned beef for healthy protein

parts.note: a soldier is one caste of ant, so an ant is possibly a soldier
one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: one piece taking another in means it holds it inside itself

parts.note: canned food is tinned, giving tin
an ox is a beef animal

explanation.surface: A soldier eating a tin of corned beef to keep his strength up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soldier, possibly' is a definition by example: soldiers are one caste of ant colonies.
explanation.definitionFit: An antitoxin is an antibody, a protein the body makes to neutralise a poison and keep it well.

clue.text: It's said very quickly and may be cutting

definitions.meaning: the British idiom 'before you could say ...' with this word means instantly, so the word is what gets said very quickly
a bladed tool used for cutting

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition relies on the old British phrase for something done in a flash; the second is the plain tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A blade is the tool you cut with, and the word is the one spoken in the idiom for great speed.

clue.text: Chair duly fixed, operating under pressure

indicators.note: something fixed has been rearranged or doctored, so the letters are reset

explanation.surface: A chair has been properly repaired and is running again under strain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fixed' rearranges the letters of CHAIR DULY.
explanation.definitionFit: Hydraulic machinery works by fluid pressure, so it is literally powered under pressure.

clue.text: Touching down, a plane between flights

definitions.meaning: the arrival of an aircraft on the ground
a flat floor area between two flights of stairs

explanation.walkthrough: 'plane' and 'flights' suggest aircraft, but the second sense is a level surface between staircases.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft's arrival on the runway, and the flat stretch on a staircase between sets of steps.

clue.text: Wisdom of husband keeping up small section of business

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece keeping another up sits beneath it

parts.note: dept is the short form of department, a section of a business

explanation.surface: A husband shows wisdom by propping up a small part of the firm.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, H 'keeping up' DEPT means H sits under it.
explanation.definitionFit: Depth of understanding is profundity, a synonym for great wisdom or insight.

clue.text: Lieutenant backing out of expensive cover

indicators.note: a piece taken out of a word is removed from it

parts.note: something costly is expensive

indicators.note: backing means the abbreviation is read backwards

explanation.surface: An officer withdrawing from an overpriced insurance policy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns LT into TL, which 'out of' removes from COSTLY.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea or egg warmer is a padded cover that keeps the pot hot.

clue.text: Periodical writer?

parts.note: suggests someone who writes now and then, but really someone who writes regularly for a periodical, a newspaper or magazine

explanation.definitionFit: Such a journalist writes a regular feature in a periodical publication.

clue.text: Grim end for sailors.

definitions.meaning: the rear of a ship, the end that sailors know as aft

explanation.definitionFit: Severe and unsmiling, and also the back part of a boat.

clue.text: Walked purposefully, using gun to cover freed duke

indicators.note: one piece covering another goes around it

parts.note: the Sten is a British submachine gun
rid means freed, as in 'rid of'

explanation.surface: A man strides off with a gun to guard a duke he has released.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sten was a cheap British submachine gun of the Second World War.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the past participle of stride, to walk with long purposeful steps.

clue.text: Friend allowed on mattress

parts.note: a pal is a friend
let means allowed

explanation.surface: A friend is permitted to sleep on the mattress.
explanation.definitionFit: A straw-filled bed or makeshift mattress on the floor is an old meaning of the word.

clue.text: Divine female has final article rejected

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as printed: 'Divine female has final article rejected (6)'. ATHENA reads as A + THE + rev(AN), but no clue words give A or THE: only 'final article rejected' (NA) has words, so the parse cannot be written.
annotationWithheld.clue: Divine female has final article rejected

clue.text: Cruel to bury a nag's head in it

indicators.note: the pieces go in it, inside the verb meaning to bury

parts.note: to inhume is to bury, the opposite of exhume

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A heartless instruction to bury a horse's head in something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in it' puts A + N (first letter of 'nag's') into INHUME.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking pity or kindness to others, so heartless.

clue.text: Times editor with leading article made cuts

indicators.note: the first letter of the word it picks from

parts.note: the indefinite article a, placed at the front
x is the multiplication sign, read as times

explanation.surface: The Times editor, with a front-page editorial, has trimmed the copy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading article' is a newspaper editorial in the surface, but here an article (A) that leads.
explanation.definitionFit: Chopped or cut, past tense, as with jobs or spending that have been reduced.

clue.text: Continue tediously, knowing it's an insect

parts.note: to drag on is to continue tediously
fly is British slang for knowing or shrewd

explanation.surface: Something goes on and on, aware that it's just a bug.
explanation.walkthrough: FLY meaning sharp or streetwise is British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A large, long-bodied flying creature of ponds and rivers, a kind of bug.

clue.text: It's unusually rational without concerning management

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so one word goes around another

parts.note: logical means rational

indicators.note: unusually signals the letters appear in an unusual order

explanation.surface: Being rational without worrying about management is odd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but here has its old sense of 'outside'; 'unusually' rearranges IT'S.
explanation.definitionFit: It describes the organising of supplies and operations, so relating to administration of resources.

clue.text: Extended fare from this junction?

parts.note: long strands of pasta, and also the nickname of a tangled motorway interchange in Birmingham

explanation.walkthrough: The Gravelly Hill Interchange on the M6 in Birmingham is nicknamed after this long pasta.
explanation.definitionFit: Long thin pasta, and the British nickname for a famously knotted road junction.

clue.text: In university not a star, but otherwise one goes far

indicators.note: the university letter goes in the rearranged letters
otherwise signals the letters are put another way

explanation.surface: Someone at university is no star student but will go far in other ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'otherwise' rearranges NOT A STAR, and 'In' puts U inside the result.
explanation.definitionFit: A space traveller literally travels a very long way from Earth.

clue.text: In absurd action, sailor about to enter a freezing area

indicators.note: pieces that enter another go inside it

parts.note: an antic is a grotesque or absurd action
a tar is a sailor
c is short for circa, about

explanation.surface: A sailor clowning about on his way to an icy region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'absurd action' looks like anagram signal plus fodder, but together they define a single noun: an antic.
explanation.definitionFit: The frozen southern continent around the South Pole is the iciest region on Earth.

clue.text: Place in ground holding, say, this number

indicators.note: one piece holding another contains it

parts.note: to inter is to place in the ground, bury
eg means for example, say

explanation.surface: Burying something, say this figure, in the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this number' is a gentle self-reference: the answer is a kind of number.
explanation.definitionFit: A whole number with no fractional part is the mathematical term.

clue.text: Short skirt in Paris you intimately revealed more than once

indicators.note: the French word shows up more than once, so it appears twice in a row

parts.note: tu is the familiar French word for you

explanation.surface: In Paris, a short skirt revealed you intimately more than once.
explanation.walkthrough: French uses tu for 'you' with intimates; it is repeated.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballerina's short stiff skirt of layered net.

clue.text: Suggestive of grief once let out externally

indicators.note: one piece placed externally sits around another

parts.note: to rent is to let out a property
dole is an archaic word for grief

explanation.surface: Something that hints at grief once released outwardly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'once' marks an archaic sense, and 'let out' is a single phrase meaning to rent.
explanation.definitionFit: Reminiscent or evocative, used of something that brings a thing to mind.

clue.text: Peer's uniform

definitions.meaning: a peer is a person of the same standing as another, and 's is 'is'

explanation.definitionFit: A peer is someone of matching rank, and uniform means level or the same all through.

clue.text: It's included in deliveries to public bar

indicators.note: the letters are included in the run of words that follow

explanation.surface: It's part of the stock delivered to the public bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'included in' signals the letters inside DELIVERIES TO PUBLIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal term meaning to preclude someone from asserting something, so to prevent.

clue.text: Stolen sum of money found in dish

parts.note: hot is slang for stolen goods
a pot is a sum of money, as in a jackpot or pool

explanation.surface: Stolen cash turns up hidden in a dish.
explanation.walkthrough: Lancashire hotpot is a British stew of lamb topped with sliced potato.
explanation.definitionFit: A baked meat and potato stew, a classic northern English meal.

clue.text: Luggage at front of Jumbo

definitions.meaning: a large travelling case or chest
an elephant's long nose, at the front of Jumbo, a classic name for an elephant

explanation.definitionFit: A big travelling chest for luggage, and the elephant's long nose at its front.

clue.text: Repeatedly strike refreshment counter

definitions.meaning: to batter or pound again and again, like wind and waves
a counter serving food and drinks, as at a station

explanation.definitionFit: To batter repeatedly, and a counter or table from which snacks are served.

clue.text: As announced, Channel will become rough

indicators.note: as announced means the words are spoken aloud and heard

parts.note: a gutter is a channel, and 'will' contracts to 'll

explanation.surface: Forecasters announce that the English Channel will turn stormy.
explanation.walkthrough: GUTTER'LL said aloud gives the sound; 'Channel' is not the sea here but a drain.
explanation.definitionFit: A throaty, harsh-sounding voice is described this way, so rasping.

clue.text: Freedom of movement was the thing for Hamlet

definitions.meaning: slack or room to move, as in a loose rope
Hamlet says 'the ... 's the thing' when planning to catch the king with a staged drama

explanation.definitionFit: Slack in a mechanism, and the staged drama Hamlet uses to expose his uncle.

clue.text: Fussy English sailors interrupting patrol at end of duty

indicators.note: pieces interrupting another break into it

parts.note: a picket is a soldier or small group on patrol or guard
RN is the Royal Navy, sailors

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Particular English sailors cut in on a patrol at the close of their shift.
explanation.walkthrough: A picket can be a soldier or small group sent out on guard or patrol duty.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessively particular about small details, so finicky.
